scope: Corollary 6.4 (Curvature rates in a fixed dimension) of the manuscript “A closed Ricci flow with bounded scalar curvature and finite-time curvature blowup” (preprints/A-closed-Ricci-flow-with-bounded-scalar-curvature-and-finite-time-curvature-blowup-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 351 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 88b1d8270cb2bc5f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 19. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every sufficiently large integer q, set dq = q + 1 − p (q + 1)(q − 7) 2 . For every sufficiently large even integer k, with the threshold allowed to depend on q, there is a smooth Ricci flow on S2 × Sq+1 with finite maximal time T, uniformly bounded scalar curvature, and constants 0 < c ≤ C < ∞ such that c(T − t)−2k/dq ≤ max M | Rm |(·, t) ≤ C(T − t)−2k/dq for all sufficiently late times. In particular, one fixed dimension admits such flows with an unbounded discrete set of power-law Type-II curvature exponents. The flow, T, and the constants may depend on q and k.
